title: Care Assistant
company: Hamberley Care Management Limited - Company - Permanent
description:
Be all you can be with Hamberley
At Hamberley, we believe that our residents deserve something 'Extra Special, Every Day' and we're recruiting for a Care Assistant to help us achieve our goals.
At Nesbit House our Care Assistants are called Homemakers. More than support workers, care assistants or healthcare assistants - they are carers and companions all in one. They have the time to get to know our residents and are trusted to give each person the care they need, in the way they like.
Joining us at Nesbit House, our luxury care home that provides residential, dementia, and nursing care for older people, you'll be part of a team that is genuinely passionate about the health and well-being of our residents.
Working Pattern: 12 hour shifts and working alternate weekends on a rota basis.
We offer our colleagues
- A competitive salary and benefits package
- 28 days holiday inclusive of Bank Holidays
- Quality-linked bonus scheme - A performance bonus tied to our CQC/CI quality rating, rewarding you for helping us deliver outstanding care.
- Workplace pension for your future security
- A true team culture - A collaborative, encouraging working environment where kindness, respect, and professional pride are at the heart of everything we do
- Excellent training and career development opportunities
- Employee Assistance Programme, occupational health and wellbeing support services
- Everyday saving perks - Access to a wide range of retail discounts and savings
- Free on-site parking
- Rewarding connections - Refer a Friend bonus - earn up to £750 per successful referral because great people know great people.

Be different - be a Homemaker
Be at the heart of our award winning homemaker care mode. A Homemaker is a unique caring role for a unique person, where you can care with a difference.
- A varied role where no two days are the same. Homemakers, our name for care assistants, care for individual people in the way a family member might care for someone in their home. We don't do timetabled task-based care - we care for each individual in the way that works best for them. Whether that's administering medication, helping make someone's bed, arranging a family meal with their loved ones or taking them to the beauty salon, you'll always be doing something different. Our Homemakers focus on the tiny details that make our residents unique, and tailor care to each and every individual.
- A chance to make a real difference to our residents' lives. Often healthcare assistants, care assistants and domiciliary care assistants find they don't get to spend enough time with the people they care for to make a real difference. Not at Hamberley. As a Homemaker you have fewer people to care for, but you spend more time with them. It's a more satisfying and fulfilling role that is better for our residents. That's why the model has won awards.
- Excellent opportunities for learning and development. We will support you with all the training you need, including NVQ qualifications and further clinical training if you want to specialise in areas like dementia and nutrition.
- Supportive team environment. Being kind and supportive to each other is key to our ability to show kindness and companionship to our residents. We truly believe this across all parts of our organisation. It's just one of the reasons that, when people join us, they stay with us.

Could you be part of our team?
We provide full training and induction, so we're more interested in you as a person than your specific care experience.
You may have experience as a healthcare assistant, care assistant, carer, home care assistant or domiciliary care assistant and are looking for a different approach, a nicer work environment and a more satisfying role.
If you have no work experience in care but are interested in helping people live happy lives, we'll guide you to a fantastic care assistant career at Hamberley.
What is important is that you have passion, empathy and dedication to help our residents live their lives to the fullest. We will support you with everything else!
If this sounds like you and you're looking for a fulfilling role that makes a genuine impact in the lives of others, this rewarding career is for you.
Due to the high level of interest we anticipate for this role, we may close this advert earlier than the stated closing date to manage applications effectively. If you're interested in joining us at Hamberley, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
About Nesbit House
Nesbit House is a luxurious care home in Sevenoaks, Kent, part of the award-winning Hamberley Care Homes - offering luxury care homes in beautiful locations throughout the UK. Residents live in spacious, stylish ensuite rooms, and enjoy beautifully furnished shared spaces and landscaped gardens. From the deluxe picture house - where we screen classic films - to the on-site luxury spa - offering hairdressing, manicures and relaxing therapies - everything has been designed and finished with the care and attention you would expect from a 5-star hotel.
Hamberley People
We respect and value our residents and each other. At Hamberley Care Homes, we believe in the importance of what we do and why we do it. Creative and empowered, our people see every day as an opportunity for growth and development. We make ideas happen. Together we can achieve anything.
Be part of something special. Be part of Hamberley.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker Supported Living

Location: Gillingham, Kent
Salary: £12.71 per hour
Hours: Full-time / Part-time / Bank
Shift Pattern: Days, evenings, weekends and bank holidays as required
Contract: Permanent, zero hours

Make a Difference. Support Independence. Change Lives.

We are looking for compassionate, resilient, and motivated Support Workers to join our team supporting vulnerable adults and individuals with previous offending histories within a supported living environment.

This is a rewarding role where you will help individuals develop their independence, build confidence, maintain their accommodation, engage with their community, and work towards achieving their personal goals.

You will be supporting people with a range of needs and life experiences. This may include individuals who have experienced homelessness, mental health challenges, substance misuse, social exclusion, offending behaviour, or difficulties maintaining independent living.

The Role

As a Support Worker, you will provide person-centred, trauma-informed and strengths-based support, helping residents develop the skills and confidence they need to live as independently as possible.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing practical, emotional and social support to residents
- Supporting individuals with daily living skills, including cooking, budgeting, cleaning and maintaining their accommodation
- Encouraging independence and positive decision-making
- Supporting residents to develop healthy routines and positive relationships
- Working in accordance with individual support plans, risk assessments and behavioural support plans
- Recognising and responding appropriately to safeguarding concerns
- Supporting individuals to manage challenging situations and reduce the risk of crisis
- Promoting positive risk-taking while maintaining appropriate boundaries
- Maintaining accurate records, case notes and incident reports
- Encouraging residents to take responsibility for their own choices and progress
- Promoting equality, dignity, respect and inclusion at all times

About You

We are looking for someone who is non-judgemental, patient and able to build positive professional relationships with people who may have complex needs or challenging life experiences.

You will ideally have:
- Experience working in supported living, social care, mental health, homelessness, rehabilitation, substance misuse, probation or a related setting
- A genuine commitment to supporting vulnerable adults
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- The ability to remain calm and professional in challenging situations
- Good understanding of safeguarding and professional boundaries
- The ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- A positive and solution-focused approach
- Reliability, resilience and a willingness to learn

Essential 6 month or more experience of working in the care sector within the UK

What We Offer
- Competitive salary
- Full-time, part-time and bank opportunities
- Comprehensive induction and training
- Ongoing learning and development
- Regular supervision and support
- Opportunities for career progression
- A supportive and inclusive working environment
- The opportunity to make a genuine difference to people's lives

Why Join Us?

Working with us is more than just a job. You will have the opportunity to help people move forward, develop independence and achieve positive change, while being part of a supportive team that values respect, compassion and professionalism.

If you are passionate about supporting people to overcome barriers and build a more positive future, we would love to hear from you.

title: Outreach Recovery Worker
description:
Outreach Recovery Worker Swale

Location: Swale

Salary: £26,000 per annum

About the Role

We are looking for a compassionate, motivated and resilient Outreach Recovery Worker to join our team, supporting adults aged 18+ who are experiencing issues with drugs and/or alcohol.

Working within an integrated healthcare framework, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred psychosocial interventions that empower individuals to reduce harm, build resilience and achieve sustainable recovery. You will work with people at varying stages of their recovery journey, delivering both harm reduction and abstinence-based approaches tailored to each individual's needs and goals.

As an Outreach Recovery Worker, you will manage a diverse caseload, undertaking comprehensive assessments, developing SMART recovery care plans, completing risk assessments, and delivering structured one-to-one and group interventions. You will provide practical advice, guidance and education around harm reduction, supporting individuals to make informed choices and improve their health and wellbeing.

A key part of the role is working collaboratively with a range of partner agencies, including housing providers, healthcare services, mental health teams, employment services, probation, criminal justice partners and community organisations. Through effective partnership working, you will ensure continuity of care and help individuals overcome barriers to recovery.

You will contribute to achieving service outcomes and contractual targets, maintaining accurate records and ensuring all interventions are delivered in line with safeguarding, governance and quality standards.

This is a flexible role and may include occasional evening and weekend working. You may also be required to travel to other services within the local cluster to ensure continuity of care and meet the needs of the people we support.

About You

You are passionate about supporting people to make positive changes in their lives and believe in a strengths-based, recovery-focused approach. You are able to build trusting relationships quickly, communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds, and remain calm and professional in challenging situations.

You will bring experience of working within substance misuse or related health and social care services, alongside a strong understanding of recovery, harm reduction and safeguarding. You will be confident managing a caseload, carrying out comprehensive assessments, developing SMART care plans and delivering structured psychosocial interventions.

We're looking for someone who has:
- Experience working within substance misuse services or a closely related field.
- Knowledge of opioid substitution treatment (OST), harm reduction principles and the wider Recovery Agenda.
- Experience completing comprehensive assessments, risk management plans and person-centred SMART care plans.
- Experience delivering structured one-to-one interventions and facilitating therapeutic group sessions.
- Confidence using motivational interviewing techniques to support behaviour change.
- A good understanding of safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries and risk management.
- Knowledge of the challenges faced by people experiencing drug and alcohol dependency and the ability to respond with empathy and professionalism.
- Experience working collaboratively with partner agencies to provide holistic, integrated support.
- A commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion, ensuring services are accessible and responsive to individual needs.
- Strong organisational, communication and IT skills, with the ability to maintain accurate case records and outcome data.
- Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends and travel across local services when required.

If you are committed to making a genuine difference in people's lives and want to be part of a supportive, values-driven organisation that believes recovery is possible for everyone, we would love to hear from you.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

We are committed to our cause and the work we carry out as a charity. Equally the wellbeing and the employees who work for us are also important. Joining us an employee, we will offer you the following benefits -
- Flexible working
- Support for Families We support our employees through every stage of family life by offering enhanced maternity and paternity pay for eligible employees who have completed 26 weeks' continuous service, alongside family-friendly policies and a supportive, inclusive workplace.
- Training and development opportunities
- Simply Health Cashback Scheme (optional)

- Contributory Pension Scheme Employer matched contributions of up to 6% in the first two years service and up to 9% thereafter
- Death in Service Payment (2x annual salary)
- Critical Illness Insurance (subject to qualifying criteria)

Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.
